## Triage: first grade, `bug` · `priority:p3` · `domain:ui` · `area:workflow` · `pm:queue`

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-10T02:21Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Lane:** the B1 page and its details rendering are objectui's (`a368ccb1a`, objectui#12045's build round), so this is `domain:ui`.
- **Why p3:** the same as objectui#12045. The page is readable, and the header names the submitter. Only the "More details" section prints internal state.
- **What the value is:** on objectstack `main`, `sys_approval_request.pending_approvers` is a `Field.textarea` (`plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts`, about `:291`). It holds the stored approver slots. So the generic details section prints it verbatim, and one id three times is one approver's quorum slots.
- **Direction:**
  - The page does not print the raw slot store. It names the pending approvers, each person once. Or, if the decision panel already names them, it hides the field from the details section.
  - ⛔ No client parsing of the slot format beyond what a published helper exposes. Measure first.
- **Two hosts:** objectstack-ai/objectstack#22473 (in flight) authors a platform `sys_approval_request_detail` page on the v18 line. cloud stays on framework `56bf27affb` until C7, so it keeps this page.
  - The claimant reads which page renders on each host.
  - If the platform page needs the same hide, that is a pointer for #22473's seat, not a change to the in-flight card.

Claim: PM loop round 3
Session: `session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8`
Account: `os-support-ai`
Branch: `claude/issue-12077-pending-approver-names`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-12077`
Domain: `domain:ui`
Seat: `domain:ui#3`
File surface (on `main` `1b2d0160`). The routed approval request page (`approvalRequestRoutes` in `apps/console/src/AppContent.tsx`, from objectui#12045's build round `a368ccb1`) prints `sys_approval_request.pending_approvers` verbatim under "More details": one id once per quorum slot. Triage's direction (`6092668487`): name the pending approvers, each person once; or, if the page already names them, hide the field from the details section. ⛔ No client parsing of the slot format beyond what a published helper exposes.
- **Measure first, then take the smaller route the measurement allows:**
  - **(a) Name each pending approver once** where the details section draws `pending_approvers`, on the request page only. Resolve the ids to names with one batched read per page (the way objectui#12067 resolved `actor_id`), and de-duplicate. The console's inbox (`apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx`, about `:271`) already resolves `pending_approvers` to people: reuse its reading, or the published helper it uses, not a second parser.
  - **(b) Hide the field from the details section** on the request page, if the page already names the pending approvers elsewhere. The dev reads what the routed page draws today, including whether `DecisionProgressIndicator` or the declared actions name them.
- The files the dev may touch, each named in the report before editing:
  - the route's own page wiring in `apps/console/src/AppContent.tsx`;
  - the approvals source `apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.ts`, read-side only, ⛔ never dropping a field the record carries;
  - the details renderer path the measurement shows draws the field (`packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailSection.tsx` or `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`).
- The tests beside these. Pins:
  - one approver holding three slots renders one name;
  - two approvers render two names;
  - control: another object's record page is unchanged.
- One `.changeset/12077-*.md` (`patch`).

⛔ Not on it:
- the slot format itself, and any server change: objectstack-ai/objectstack#22473's platform page is the v18 host. If that page needs the same treatment, the seat leaves a pointer there and does not change the in-flight card;
- the decision panel's registration (objectui#12045's page-mount step);
- `packages/i18n/**` (a new key is a stop) and `packages/components/src/ui/**`.

If neither (a) nor (b) can be done without parsing the slot format or adding a published prop or export, stop and report with measured options.
Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (`dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui` over these paths: no path-derived mandate; default tier).
Clause-②: no
Responsibility: `objectui console: the routed sys_approval_request record page prints pending_approvers' raw slot store (one id per quorum slot) under More details, while its header names the submitter | the platform path: the inbox's existing approver resolution, or the page's own naming of the approvers | every user who opens an approval request on the routed page`
Thread-read: 6092668487
Serial constraints cleared: `none` blocking.
- **Open objectui PRs, read 2026-10-10T02:48Z:** none touches these files.
- **objectui#12045** (`pm:blocked`, claim released) owns the request page's mount step; this card fixes what the page draws today.
- **In-flight claims, read 2026-10-10T02:48Z:** none in this repo carries `pm:dispatched` (serial dispatch).

Why `Clause-②: no`: a display fix on one console route, with no export, prop, type or pack key changed. If the route needs one, that is a stop.

Seat decision — `domain:ui` seat 3, `session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8`, 2026-10-10T03:09Z. State: `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked` in this act, with the claim released. Answers the dev's stop (report on this card; no code, no PR).

**What the dev measured** (the real `RecordDetailView` over the routed approvals source):
- "More details" prints `pending_approvers` as the raw id three times, and no approver is named anywhere on the routed page.
- **Route (b), hiding the field only, fails its precondition:** nothing else on the page names a pending approver.
  - The decision panel is not mounted there; its registration waits for objectui#12045's page-mount step.
  - The approvals hook and `DeclaredActionsBar` are off on a request's own page.
  - Hiding the field (`hidden: true` in the route's objects list) removes the row and leaves no approver named at all.
- **Route (a) has no in-place hook inside the claim:** each one retypes a declared field, rewrites a field the record carries, or adds a cell-registry key.
- **Correction to the claim:** the get route already serves `pending_approver_names` (id to name, one batched `sys_user` lookup on the server), so naming needs no extra client read. Only user-id slots get a name. `position:` / `role:` slots resolve through app-shell's existing approver directory.

**Decision: A, carried as A1.** These are order-of-steps and technical-route choices inside triage's direction (`6092668487`: name each person once, or hide only where the page already names them). No product question is decided, and the maintainer's veto window is open.
- **A:** the page names the approvers where it already reads the approvals contract. The decision panel names each pending approver once through app-shell's existing single source (`approverChips` over `pending_approver_names` and the approver directory), and then the raw slot store is hidden from the request page's details.
  - Both halves land **with or after objectui#12045's page-mount step**, so the hide never ships without the names.
  - The hide is route-scoped (the console route's objects override, measured to remove only this row), or producer-side if the page-mount measurement prefers it.
- **A1:** this card stays, `pm:blocked` on objectui#12045, and is claimed afresh once the page mounts. Its pins (three slots render one name; two approvers render two names; another object's page is unchanged) stay separately reviewable.
- ⛔ **Not B,** a 17.x interim cell face. It adds a single-use cell-registry key and an object branch to a generic view, it is retired at the v18 cutover, and the startup rule keeps transitions tight with no staged route. Reach today is rig-only, per the card.
- ⛔ **Not C** (hide only: the page would name no approver, against triage's direction). ⛔ **Not D** (rewriting a field the record carries; the panel and the override confirm read the ids).

**Release:** `session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8` (account `os-support-ai`) releases the claim `6092974406`.
- **Reason:** the fix waits for objectui#12045's page-mount step.
- **Destination:** `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by: #12045` in the body. The unlock scan returns the card when objectui#12045 closes. The next claim's surface:
  - the decision panel (`packages/app-shell/src/views/approval-decision/`), naming approvers through app-shell's `approverChips` single source;
  - the request route's hide of `pending_approvers`;
  - the three pins above.
- The branch `claude/issue-12077-pending-approver-names` stays on the remote, empty, for reuse.

**Host note (not filed):**
- objectstack-ai/objectstack#22567's v18 page puts a bare `record:details` in its Details tab. By the dev's code reading, that tab prints the same raw store. This was not browser-measured.
- The route-scoped hide covers it when the page renders through the console route. The re-claim measures it on the served page.
